item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antipsychotic

lookback_source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period, or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days. Per the general convention, the ARD is day 1 counting back (ARD + 6 previous calendar days). Column 1 (N0415A1) and Column 2 (N0415A2) both use the 7-day look-back/observation period.

coding_levels.label: Is taking — Antipsychotic
coding_levels.definition: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Indication noted — Antipsychotic
coding_levels.definition: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A2. Antipsychotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

coding_levels.label: Not checked
coding_levels.definition: Boxes for "check all that apply" items remain blank when the specified condition is not met (general convention). Example: N0415D2 Hypnotic = not checked because indication for use was not noted.

source.quote: Use a check mark for boxes where the instructions state to "check all that apply," if the specified condition is met; otherwise, these boxes should remain blank

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415A1 if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check N0415A2 if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415A2. Antipsychotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as antianxiety, not hypnotic).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification are coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how used (e.g., prochlorperazine, dually classified as antipsychotic and antiemetic, is coded as an antipsychotic).

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, given every few weeks or monthly, only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination (e.g., a single tablet combining an antipsychotic and an antidepressant is coded in both antipsychotic and antidepressant categories).

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are not counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Coding example: risperidone received PRN on 3 days for bipolar disorder with indication noted results in N0415A1 and N0415A2 Antipsychotic both checked.

source.quote: N0415A1 and N0415A2. Antipsychotic = checked; risperidone is an antipsychotic medication and indication of use for bipolar disorder noted.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Skip logic into N0415: if N0300 (Injections) is coded 0, skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication.

source.quote: If 0 → Skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: An indication is the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals; Column 2 requires such an indication be noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box on the same page as the coding instructions.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0 for pharmacological classification; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that sources are identifiable.

federal.criterion: Assessors may consult the manufacturer's package insert or work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm medication classification(s).

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification.

federal.notes: Suggested resource, not a required document.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives antipsychotic, antianxiety, and hypnotic medications simultaneously, adequate documentation of a clear clinical indication is essential to justify their use.

source.quote: Please note: if a resident is receiving medications in all three of these high-risk drug classes simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication for the use of these medications.

federal.notes: Stated in the note following the N0415 example; the manual adds "Adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use."

case_mix_relevance.notes: The N0415 pages do not tie this item to a payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Whether N0415A2 (Column 2, indication noted) is limited to residents whose Column 1 box is checked

positions.claim: Column 2 is completed only if Column 1 is checked.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

positions.claim: The N0415A2 bullet states the check condition without restating the Column 1 precondition.

source.quote: N0415A2. Antipsychotic: Check if there is an indication noted for all antipsychotic medications taken by the resident any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Not a substantive disagreement: the item-level instruction on p. N-6 states the Column 1 precondition that governs all Column 2 sub-items, including N0415A2.
